title: host_of() disagrees with the browser on backslash-userinfo URLs: resolve() releases the secret for 'https://evil.test\@pathlynks.test', which Chromium (WHATWG) navigates to evil.test
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:60-63 host_of uses urllib.parse.urlparse, which treats 'evil.test\\' as userinfo and returns hostname 'pathlynks.test'. WHATWG URL (what Chromium/Playwright implement; verified with node `new URL(...)`): backslash is a path separator in special schemes, so host='evil.test', path='/@pathlynks.test'. Probe: SecretStore(proj(domains=['pathlynks.test']),{'PW':'supersecretvalue'}).resolve('{{SECRET:PW}}','https://evil.test\\@pathlynks.test') RETURNED the value. B3 says scoping is enforced against the current page host; here the page host would be evil.test. Note: 'https://evil.test%2F@pathlynks.test' is consistent on both parsers (host pathlynks.test) and is NOT a leak; the cycle-1 userinfo probe ('a.test@evil.test') was the safe direction. Fix direction (fail closed, two lines): in host_of() return '' when the raw input contains a backslash or when urlparse yields a username/password (any userinfo) — an empty host already raises SecretScopeError since AT-001. Add both as tests. T-010 must additionally pass the browser's own page.url (post-navigation) to resolve(), never the step's intended URL. CYCLE-3 RE-CHECK: host_of (secrets.py:73-88) returns '' on any backslash or any urlparse userinfo; resolve() raises SecretScopeError on ''. Cross-checked 35 destinations against node v24 `new URL(...).hostname`: every case where urlparse and WHATWG disagree in the leak direction ('evil.test\@pathlynks.test', 'pathlynks.test@evil.test', 'https:\\pathlynks.test', 'evil.test:@pathlynks.test', '@pathlynks.test', U+2044 userinfo) now returns '' (refused). Remaining disagreements ('pathlynks%2Etest', 'pathlynks．test', trailing-space host) are all in the safe direction (refused while the browser would visit the legit host). Pinned by test_at007_backslash_and_userinfo_destinations_fail_closed.
